challenge.method: Checked the operative version sentence against the included heading, section 13 and the “any later version” sample notice. Also checked the historical reference to GNU Library GPL version 2 and the role of clause 2 in the modified-version condition.
challenge.results: The later-version wording occurs in guidance for licensing new libraries. Section 13 describes the election when a library specifies it. The OCaml notice itself specifies version 2.1 without that election. The reference to Library GPL version 2 describes a predecessor. Clause 2 qualifies the modified distribution, while clause 6 identifies the additional requirements addressed by the exception.

limitations: The supported edition is the expressly named LGPL version 2.1 for this defined Core System. The relationship does not establish a project-wide license expression, compatibility finding or release history.
The clause 6 permission has the linking, distribution and public-version qualifications in the inline paragraph. Other grounds for LGPL coverage remain possible.
reasoning: The OCaml project's operative notice expressly places its defined Core System under “GNU Lesser General Public License (LGPL) version 2.1 (included below).” The included license heading confirms Version 2.1, February 1999. The adjacent exception expressly refers to additional requirements in clause 6, and the included clause 6 addresses combining or linking a work that uses the Library and distributing the result. This supports the documented base relationship at the named commit.
